title: Enforce immutable local-only runtime configuration
verify: Independent verification proves only literal local_only starts, representative future/server statuses fail before app startup, and safe failure output contains no rejected secret/config value.

verify.summary: Adversarial probes: hostile/coerced/env-injected values all rejected via kwargs+from_env, value never in str/repr/traceback; subprocess import fails before routes; no model_construct/parse bypass; all script paths use from_env (same validator); no surface creep (config.py +10/-1 + new test); invariants and Constitution fit; no admitted findings.

evidence_required: FT-015-AC-001 RED: AppSettings currently accepts an arbitrary SYNC_STATUS such as server_verified; GREEN: only literal local_only validates and representative server/upload values fail before create_app; decisive comparison: settings/app construction result and safe error text; artifact: focused pytest transcript under .tasks/TASK-062-T3-FT-015-W1/.
purpose: Turn the documented local_only invariant into fail-closed executable configuration so no MVP startup can silently accept a future server/upload sync state.
success_outcome: AppSettings accepts the default or explicit literal local_only and rejects every other sync status before application startup without leaking the rejected value; existing local runtime roots and Foundation smoke behavior remain compatible.
anti_goals: Do not add a sync lifecycle, server target, upload state, migration, API, frontend, or remote I/O.
Do not change local runtime roots or Foundation health/readiness behavior.
constraints: Use the smallest settings-level literal validation; no enum/lifecycle abstraction beyond the one accepted value.
Preserve AppSettings test injection and redacted_for_log behavior.
invariants: MVP sync authority is always local_only.
Invalid configuration fails before product routes can serve.
verification_targets: FT-015-AC-001: focused settings/app tests compare arbitrary-status pre-RED with literal-only GREEN and prove no sync mutation surface.

forbidden_scope: Remote/server sync, upload orchestration, database schema, PWA/frontend, provider configuration, or historical task evidence.
stop_conditions: Rejecting non-local_only requires a new product lifecycle or changes an existing public response.
The supported Foundation start/settings injection path cannot be preserved.
